athletics = track and field sports such as running, jumping and throwing
gymnastics = a sport of exercises on the floor and apparatus that need strength, balance and control
martial arts = combat sports such as judo, karate or taekwondo
extreme sports = sports with a high level of danger or adrenaline, such as climbing or rafting
motorsport = competitive racing in cars, motorbikes or similar vehicles
triathlon = a race combining swimming, cycling and running
pentathlon = a contest of five events, in the modern form including fencing and riding
weightlifting = a sport of lifting a loaded bar from the ground to above the head
archery = the sport of shooting arrows at a target with a bow
fencing = a combat sport using a foil, épée or sabre
rowing = the sport of racing boats that are moved with oars
canoeing = paddling a canoe, often as a race or on fast water
windsurfing = riding a board with a sail, using the wind on water
scuba diving = swimming underwater with a tank of compressed air
rock climbing = climbing natural rock faces using hands, feet and safety gear
mountaineering = climbing high mountains, often with ice, snow and altitude
bouldering = climbing short, difficult routes without a rope, using crash mats
parkour = moving through a city or course by jumping, climbing and vaulting
figure skating = ice skating that combines jumps, spins and dance steps
biathlon = a winter sport combining cross-country skiing and rifle shooting
ski jumping = skiing down a ramp and jumping as far as possible
curling = a sport on ice in which teams slide stones towards a target
water polo = a team ball game played in a pool, similar to handball in water
synchronised swimming = a sport in which swimmers perform a routine of movements to music
orienteering = finding your way across country with a map and compass against the clock
show jumping = a riding event in which horse and rider jump a course of fences
snooker = a cue sport played with 21 balls on a large table, popular in Britain
netball = a team game similar to basketball, widely played in British schools
field hockey = a team game played with sticks and a ball on grass or artificial turf
rugby union = a 15-a-side rugby code with scrums, lineouts and tries worth five points
stadium = a large sports ground with seats around the playing area
pitch = the marked grass or turf area where football or rugby is played
court = the marked area for tennis, basketball, volleyball or squash
athletics track = the oval running surface used for track events
arena = a large indoor venue for sport or entertainment
velodrome = a track, often banked, designed for cycle racing
ice rink = an ice surface for skating, ice hockey or curling
ski slope = a prepared hillside used for skiing or snowboarding
golf course = an area of land with numbered holes for playing golf
sports hall = an indoor hall marked for several sports, often at a school
changing room = a room where players change clothes before and after sport
dugout = the shelter beside the pitch where the coach and substitutes sit
grandstand = the main, often covered, stand with the best seats
floodlights = powerful lights that allow sport to be played after dark
sports venue = a place designed for sport, such as a stadium, pool or hall
gym = a place with equipment for physical training
racket = the strung implement used to hit the ball or shuttlecock
helmet = a hard hat that protects the head in cycling, skating or riding
shin pads = guards worn on the lower legs, especially in football
gumshield = a plastic guard worn in the mouth to protect the teeth
goggles = protective glasses for swimming, skiing or cycling
wetsuit = a close-fitting rubber suit that keeps you warm in cold water
trainers = comfortable sports shoes for running or the gym
football boots = studded shoes designed for football or rugby on grass
spikes = running shoes with metal points for grip on a track
stopwatch = a watch used to measure exact times in training or races
scoreboard = a board that displays the score and sometimes the time
goalposts = the two upright posts, and usually a bar, that form a goal
shuttlecock = the feathered or plastic object hit in badminton
puck = the hard rubber disc used in ice hockey
barbell = a long bar with weights at each end, used for lifting
dumbbells = short bars with weights, held in each hand
treadmill = a machine with a moving belt that you run or walk on
harness = straps worn around the body and attached to a rope for safety
oar = a long pole with a blade, used to row a boat
ski poles = poles used for balance and push on skis
fixture = a scheduled match in a competition
tournament = a series of games that continue until there is a winner
championship = a competition to decide the best team or player in a sport
qualifying round = an early stage that decides who reaches the main competition
league = a group of clubs that play one another over a season
cup tie = a match in a knockout cup competition
quarter-final = a match whose winner reaches the last four
semi-final = a match whose winner goes through to the final
play-off = an extra match or series to decide promotion, qualification or a title
derby = a match between two clubs from the same city or region
friendly = a match that does not count in a league or cup
extra time = additional playing time when a knockout match is still a draw
penalty shoot-out = taking turns at penalties to decide a drawn knockout match
Olympic Games = the world's largest multi-sport event, held every four years
Paralympic Games = the major international multi-sport event for athletes with disabilities
Grand Slam = one of the four major tennis tournaments, or winning all four in a year
world record = the best official result ever achieved in an event
knockout stage = the part of a tournament in which losing means elimination
group stage = the opening round in which teams play in small groups
opening ceremony = the official show that starts a major championship or Games
medal ceremony = the official presentation of medals after an event
seeded player = a highly ranked competitor given a favourable place in the draw
heat = an early race that decides who reaches the next round
kick-off = the first kick that starts a football match; the scheduled start time
referee = the official who controls a football, rugby or boxing contest
umpire = the official who controls tennis, cricket, volleyball or badminton
assistant referee = an official who helps the referee, especially with offside and throw-ins
substitute = a player who comes on in place of a teammate
spectator = a person who watches a sports event in person
hooligan = a person who causes violence or damage in connection with sport
coach = a person who trains a team or athlete
manager = the person in charge of a football club's team affairs
captain = the player who leads the team on the field
goalkeeper = the player whose job is to stop the ball going into the goal
striker = a forward whose main job is to score goals
defender = a player whose main job is to stop the other team scoring
midfielder = a player who links defence and attack in the middle of the pitch
sports commentator = a person who describes a match live on television or radio
pundit = a former player or expert who analyses sport on television
scout = a person who watches players to find talent for a club
physio = a physiotherapist who treats sports injuries
steward = a person who helps with safety and crowd control at a venue
supporter = a person who regularly follows and backs a particular team
sports agent = a person who represents an athlete in contracts and transfers
amateur = a person who plays sport without being paid as a professional
professional = a person who is paid to play sport as their job
stamina = the ability to keep exercising hard for a long time
personal best = your own fastest or best result in an event
warm-up = gentle exercise done before a hard session or match
cool-down = gentle exercise after sport so the body recovers gradually
circuit training = a session of short exercises done one after another at stations
interval training = alternating bursts of hard effort with recovery periods
weight training = exercise using weights to build strength
endurance = the ability to keep going in long-lasting physical effort
agility = the ability to change direction quickly and under control
coordination = the ability to use different parts of the body together smoothly
flexibility = how far your joints and muscles can stretch
recovery = the process of the body repairing itself after training
overtraining = training so hard or so often that performance and health get worse
carbohydrate loading = eating extra carbohydrates before a long event to store energy
energy drink = a drink with caffeine and sugar, marketed to boost alertness or performance
hydration = keeping enough fluid in the body during exercise
tapering = reducing training load shortly before a competition so you arrive fresh
cross-training = doing a different sport to support your main one and reduce injury
personal trainer = a coach who designs and supervises exercise for an individual
training camp = a period when athletes live and train together, often away from home
pre-season = the training period before the competitive season starts
off-season = the period when there is no official competition
peak fitness = the highest level of condition an athlete can reach for a target event
blood doping = illegally boosting performance by manipulating blood or red cells
doping = using banned substances or methods to improve sporting results
match-fixing = illegally arranging the result or events of a match, often for betting
equal pay in sport = the principle that women and men should receive comparable pay and prizes
sportsmanship = fair, respectful behaviour towards opponents and officials
sports scholarship = money given to a student because of athletic ability
fair play = playing by the rules and showing respect, even when it costs you
banned substance = a drug or chemical that athletes are not allowed to use
performance-enhancing drug = a drug taken to improve strength, speed, endurance or recovery
drug test = an official check of blood or urine for banned substances
life ban = a punishment that stops someone competing for the rest of their life
hooliganism = organised or spontaneous violence by fans around sports events
racism in sport = unfair treatment or abuse of people because of race in a sporting context
concussion = a brain injury from a blow to the head, common in contact sport
rehabilitation = the process of recovering fitness and skill after injury
VAR = video technology that helps football referees review key decisions
yellow card = a caution from the referee for unsporting behaviour or a foul
red card = a sending-off, leaving the team with one fewer player
sending-off = the act of dismissing a player from the match
gamesmanship = using legal but unsporting tricks to gain an advantage
time-wasting = deliberately slowing the game to protect a lead
diving = pretending to be fouled in order to win a free kick or penalty
transfer fee = the money one club pays another to sign a player under contract
grassroots sport = local, amateur sport that develops participation rather than elite results
elite sport = sport at the highest competitive level, usually professional
adrenaline rush = a sudden feeling of excitement caused by danger or intense effort
skydiving = jumping from an aircraft and falling before opening a parachute
white-water rafting = riding an inflatable raft down fast, rough river water
bungee jumping = jumping from a height with an elastic cord attached to the body
base jumping = parachuting from a fixed object such as a cliff or building
semi-professional = paid something to play, but not enough to live on as a full-time job
first team = the club's main senior side, not the reserves or youth team
youth academy = a club's system for training talented young players
wheelchair basketball = basketball played in sports wheelchairs, including at Paralympic level
Paralympic sport = sport organised for athletes with disabilities at elite international level
season ticket = a ticket that covers all of a team's home matches in a season
home advantage = the benefit a team gets from playing at its own ground
away fixture = a match played at the opponent's ground
league table = the ranking of clubs by points during a league season
hat-trick = three goals scored by the same player in one match
own goal = a goal accidentally scored in your own team's net
offside = a rule that a player is too far forward when the ball is played
sports psychology = the study and practice of the mental side of sporting performance
sports injury = physical damage caused by training or competition
inclusion in sport = making sport open and fair for people of different abilities, genders and backgrounds
